adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — unsubscribe changes notification settings through a GET request without CSRF protection, allowing an external site to unsubscribe an authenticated user without consent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the `unsubscribe` action is added to `topics_controller.rb` and is explicitly added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` (line 30), meaning it can be accessed without XHR. The route configuration shows `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` - this is a GET request. The action modifies `TopicUser.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, which is a state-changing operation. GET requests that modify state are vulnerable to CSRF attacks because an attacker can embed an image or link on their site that triggers the unsubscribe action when a logged-in user visits. While Rails has CSRF protection for non-GET requests, GET requests are not protected by default. This is a real security vulnerability - an external site could unsubscribe users from topics without their consent.
